requirements.name: The journey is ordered as ten sections, each a sequence of pages

scenarios.name: The journey's sections run in a fixed order
scenarios.notes: GAP: flow.js encodes ten sections (start→origin→commodities→animalIdentification→consignment→documents→addresses→transport→contact→review) but no E2E, FIT or unit asserts that product-facing order. Checked journey-smoke (opening spine only), hub-groups-and-cya-rows (Overview's six groups — a different grouping), section-captions (caption map, not flow section order), simulateJourney (page walk without naming the ten sections).

scenarios.name: The transport section sequences its pages in order

tests.test: does not ask the transporter type before the list
tests.notes: proves the type question is not offered before the combined list

tests.test: Should enter a section at its first gated-in page
tests.notes: carried over — transport enters at /port-of-entry; not re-verified this pass, and the transport section's own step list has since changed (arrival, transit, transporters only) so this test's full body needs re-reading before trusting it still matches

scenarios.notes: STALE CITATIONS REMOVED: dispatch.test.js's 'skipping the spokes the type gates out' and simulate.test.js's 'insert the gated transporter spoke exactly for the chosen type' both asserted the retired type-branches-the-section model (transporters → select/private) and no longer support this scenario's current text — not re-cited, not confirmed deleted from the suite either. No test found that walks arrival → transit → transporter-list as one sequence and asserts that specific three-step order end to end; the fit citation above only proves the type-before-list half.
